sheet-70-1.description: Main part of sheet 70, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top, covering the western end of Verona village along Bloomfield Avenue at the boundary with Essex Fells and North Caldwell. Bloomfield Avenue, 75 feet wide, crosses the middle of the sheet from west to east. Old Road branches off its north side and runs east to De Camp Place and on to the next sheet, and Forest Avenue leaves Bloomfield Avenue southward at the east edge. The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses Bloomfield Avenue on a long curve in the centre of the sheet and runs north-east toward Personette Avenue, whose corner appears at the top right. Buildings are few: scattered frame dwellings and sheds along Old Road and Bloomfield Avenue, a blacksmith, wood working and painting shop beside the railroad, and a paint shop near Old Road. The Essex Fells and North Caldwell borough lines are marked along the west edge. Much of the south and east of the part is open land, and the two upper-left and lower-left corners of the sheet are taken by separate insets at 50 feet to an inch (the American Bronze Powder Co. and the Montclair Golf Club), which are separate parts.
notes: Old Road is on the line of modern Pine Street; De Camp Place is modern Parkhurst Place (checked against sheet 71, about 5 m).
The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad is abandoned; part of its line is the West Essex Trail.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions only; the fit implies about 4.3 px/ft against about 4.04 on sheet 71, so the shallow Old Road fork or the sheet's drawing is several percent off.

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71 of the Essex County volume 3 Sanborn atlas covers the centre of Verona village on Bloomfield Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east in a gentle curve and carries most of the buildings: a row of small frame stores and dwellings on both sides between Fairview Avenue and Montrose Avenue, including a drug store, a printing shop, a coal shed, a horse shed and the Verona M. E. Church at the corner of Grove Avenue. North of Bloomfield Avenue the large lots between Fairview Avenue and Grove Avenue are mostly open, with scattered dwellings, a fish pond and a spring house, and the Verona Presbyterian Church stands on Fairview Avenue near Old Road. Personette Avenue runs along the top of the sheet, joining Fairview Avenue and Grove Avenue; De Camp Place and Old Road lie at the west edge, and Gould Street runs along the east edge to the next sheet. South of Bloomfield Avenue, Forest Avenue and S. Prospect Street lead south through deep, largely undeveloped lots; A. G. Jacobus Sons brush factory stands at the corner of Forest Avenue. A six-inch water pipe is marked on Personette Avenue and Fairview Avenue. The lower part of the sheet is blank, and adjoining sheets 70, 72 and 79 are referenced at the margins. Block numbers 1 to 5 mark the blocks.
notes: Old Road is on the line of modern Pine Street (matched at its junction with Fairview Avenue).
Grove Avenue and S. Prospect meet Bloomfield Avenue about 40 ft apart; today they meet at one junction, which was excluded from the fit.
De Camp Place appears to be on the line of modern Parkhurst Place (not used as control).
Personette and Gould are printed without a suffix; today Personette Avenue and Gould Street.

Sheet 71, 100 ft, north toward upper left (about -23 deg). Verona centre: Bloomfield Av, Fairview Av, Personette, Grove Av, Gould, Forest Av, S. Prospect, Montrose Av, De Camp Pl, Old Road. Pilot sheet. Grove Av and S. Prospect meet Bloomfield about 40 ft apart (one modern node; excluded).

sheet-72-1.description: Sheet 72 of the Essex County volume 3 Sanborn atlas shows the eastern part of Verona village along Bloomfield Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue, 75 feet wide, crosses the sheet from the west edge, where it meets Gould (north) and Montrose Avenue (south), to the east edge at Sunset Avenue. Verona Public School, a brick building, stands on the north side near the west edge and the Verona Hotel a little farther east. Peckmans Brook flows south across Bloomfield Avenue under a bridge and widens below it into Verona Lake, with an island and a dam at the upper end; the lake and its shore, marked Verona Lake Park, fill the lower middle of the sheet. East of the brook, Claremont Avenue branches from Bloomfield Avenue and Brookside Lane leads north from it. Lakeview Avenue runs south from Bloomfield Avenue to Matilda, where a row of small dwellings is built on its east side. Lakeside Avenue leads south on the west bank of the lake to Pease Avenue at the bottom left. Along the east margin Sunset Avenue runs south from Bloomfield Avenue, with the Lake View Hotel at the corner. Most of the area north and south of the main road is open or lightly built, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds on large lots. Cooks Lane and the scale bar are at the bottom. A boxed inset at the top right, Verona Lake Park with a merry-go-round, a magnetic building and a photo building, is not part of this reading; adjoining sheets 71 and 73 are referenced at the margins.
notes: Gould (north of Bloomfield) and Montrose Avenue (south) are one drawn street; the modern nodes Bloomfield Avenue / Gould Street and Bloomfield Avenue / Montrose Avenue are about 25 m apart and the Montrose node fits the drawn junction.
Sunset Avenue at the east edge of Bloomfield Avenue is Park Avenue today.
Lakeview Avenue is Lakeview Place today.

Matilda, Brookside Lane and Cooks Lane were not found in the modern street data. Claremont Avenue near Bloomfield Avenue was not used as control because the modern line does not follow the drawn fork.
Hand-picked control: Lakeside Avenue is drawn about 40 ft wide against about 80 ft in the parcels; its two junctions fit less well than the others.
Not georeferenced: the boxed inset Verona Lake Park at the top right (no street).

Sheet 72, 100 ft, north upper left (-20 deg). Verona east of centre: Bloomfield Av, Gould/Montrose Av, Lakeside Av, Lakeview Av (now Lakeview Pl), Claremont Av, Pease Av, Matilda, Brookside Lane, Sunset Av (now Park Av at Bloomfield), Verona Lake, Peckmans Brook. Part 1 main; part 2 (boxed inset, top right): Verona Lake Park, no streets.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Verona Lake Park (merry-go-round, magnetic building, photo building) (no street drawn; needs carried points from the lake outline on part 1, not tried).

sheet-73-1.description: Sheet 73 of the Essex County volume 3 Sanborn atlas covers the eastern end of Verona village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east near the middle, 75 feet wide, with blocks 1 to 10 numbered on either side. Claremont Avenue leaves the main road near the west edge and runs north-east, 50 feet wide, along the top of the central blocks. Between them lie the cross streets Claremont Place, Malvern and Hillcrest Terrace, and the Verona Congregational Church stands on the corner of Claremont Place north of Bloomfield Avenue. The north side blocks are lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots. East of Hillcrest Terrace, Elmwood Road bends north across Claremont Avenue and West View Road curves along the east margin; the narrow lots between them are laid out but only partly built. South of Bloomfield Avenue the blocks are much larger and largely open, with a few dwellings and sheds, and Brookside Avenue leads south from the main road to Sunset Avenue. Sunset Avenue enters at the lower left, runs south from Bloomfield Avenue at the west edge, then turns south-east and crosses the bottom of the sheet; Ingalls and Cooks Lane meet it at the lower left. A compass rose is printed at the upper left and the scale bar at the lower right; the neighbouring sheets 72 and 74 are referenced at the margins.
notes: Brookside Avenue is Brookdale Avenue today (matched at Bloomfield Avenue and Sunset Avenue).
Claremont Place is on the line of modern Church Street; Malvern is Malvern Place today.
The drawn Sunset Avenue at the west edge, north of its bend, is Park Avenue today; the bend itself, a skewed fork, and the Claremont Avenue / Church Street junction were excluded from the fit.
Ingalls was not found in the modern street data; the nearest modern line (Mountainview Road) is displaced from it and was left out.
Elmwood and Road, and West View and Road, are lettered on separate lines of the street: Elmwood Road and West View Road.

Sheet 73, 100 ft, north upper left (-30 deg). Bloomfield Av, Claremont Av, Claremont Pl (now Church St), Malvern (now Malvern Pl), Hillcrest Terrace, Elmwood Rd, West View Rd, Brookside Av (now Brookdale Av), Sunset Av, Ingalls, Cooks Lane.

sheet-74-1.description: Sheet 74 of the Essex County volume 3 Sanborn atlas covers the east end of Verona at the Montclair line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the lower middle of the sheet from the west edge and curves up toward the north-east corner as it nears Montclair. Claremont Avenue runs above it from the west edge to the east, and the two roads meet near the right margin. Pompton Avenue, labelled Turnpike where it runs north, comes down the middle of the sheet and ends at the two roads, with a stone quarry and a stone crusher on the wedge of land between Claremont and Bloomfield Avenues. Martin Road leads north from Claremont Avenue at the upper left, West View Road is a curved street with a row of narrow lots along the west edge, and Westover Terrace and Crestmont Road lie in the upper right, where the lots are laid out but few are built. Sunset Avenue crosses the lower half of the sheet on a diagonal from the lower left to the east edge, with Afterglow Avenue branching from it and Prospect Avenue entering at the lower left corner. Much of the sheet, including the large blocks between Bloomfield and Sunset Avenues, is open land with a handful of dwellings, a carpet cleaning and wood sawing works at the left edge and a cement block construction building near West View Road. The town line with Montclair is lettered along the east margin. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the lower right, and sheets 73 and 75 are referenced at the margins.
notes: Prospect Avenue is Mount Prospect Avenue today; Turnpike is Pompton Avenue.
The drawn Pompton Avenue ends at Bloomfield Avenue about 40 m east of the modern Bloomfield / Mount Prospect / Pompton node, so that junction was not used.
Martin Road and West View Road were left out of the fit: their modern lines do not follow the drawn ones (junctions 7 m off).
Control is four hand-picked junctions; the drawn scale fits about 2 percent larger than the atlas average.

Sheet 74, 100 ft, north upper left (-17 deg). Bloomfield and Claremont Avs at the Montclair line, Turnpike/Pompton (Pompton Av), Martin Rd, Crestmont Rd, Westover Terrace, West View Rd, Sunset Av, Afterglow Av, Prospect Av (now Mount Prospect Av), stone quarry and crusher.

sheet-75-1.description: Left half of sheet 75, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, showing the Pompton Turnpike (Pompton Avenue) running down the page through the Cedar Grove part of Verona Township, with Ridge Road branching off to the north-east near the top. The land on both sides is mostly open. Scattered frame dwellings, barns and sheds stand along the Turnpike, and the lower part is taken by Geo. H. Hastings florist and truck farm, with long greenhouses, a water tank and dwellings; a label for the Highland Varnish Co. appears at the bottom corner. A six-inch water pipe is marked along the Turnpike. The half is bounded on the right by a heavy line separating it from the right half of the sheet, which continues the Turnpike further south, and two insets sit at the top: Fabyan's Woods at 100 feet to an inch and the Highland Varnish Co. works at 50 feet to an inch, both separate parts. A north arrow is drawn on this half.
notes: The Turnpike is modern Pompton Avenue (New Jersey Route 23).
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Pompton Avenue / Ridge Road) plus a derived point; scale assumed at 4.04 px/ft and north at -14.5 degrees. Low confidence.

sheet-75-3.description: Right half of sheet 75, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continuing the Pompton Turnpike (Pompton Avenue) southward through the Cedar Grove part of Verona Township toward Claremont and Montclair. The Turnpike, 66 feet wide, runs down the right side of the half. Martin Road leaves it to the south-west in a long fork, and Westover Terrace, 30 feet wide, branches off to the east near the bottom. Near the top a long strip of lots east of the Turnpike holds the Cedar Grove Hotel and its outbuildings. Elsewhere the half shows a few frame dwellings and barns on large open lots on both sides of the Turnpike and Martin Road. A heavy line separates it from the left half of the sheet, and its own north arrow is drawn at the right edge.
notes: The Turnpike is modern Pompton Avenue; Westover Terrace is modern Westover Road.
Martin Road meets the Turnpike at a long acute fork that does not match the modern junction; it was not used.
Anchored on one junction (Pompton Avenue / Westover Road) with scale and rotation assumed. Low confidence.

sheet-76-1.description: Sheet 76 of the Essex County volume 3 Sanborn atlas covers part of Cedar Grove south of the village centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page. The Turnpike, lettered Pompton on its lower stretch and 66 feet wide, runs north and south along the left side. Near the top it meets Love Lane, which leads off to the north-east, and a brook crosses both under a bridge. The Cedar Grove Congregational Church and the Cedar Grove Public School stand on the west side of the Turnpike, with frame dwellings, a grocery and the W. M. Jenkins brush factory farther south. Cedar Avenue leaves the Turnpike and runs south-east across the middle of the sheet to a small subdivision of East Wood Place, Union and Summit streets, where about a dozen dwellings and sheds are laid out in blocks 2 and 3; H. H. Jacobus has a color printing works on the north side of Cedar Avenue. Bradford Avenue appears twice, at the bottom left and at the top right. A second stretch of the Turnpike, again lettered Pompton, runs along the right side, with Grosch Street branching off it, a gas or water pipe drawn along its margin, and R. Chestney's greenhouses and florist works beside it. A heavy double line, unlettered, runs north and south through the right half of the sheet and steps to the left at the top. The southern and eastern parts are mostly open land. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the bottom; sheets 75 and 77 are referenced at the margins.
notes: Cedar Avenue is Cedar Street today; Love Lane is Bowden Road; the Turnpike is Pompton Avenue; Union is Union Street, and East Wood Place is Eastwood Place; Summit is Summit Avenue.

Control is four junctions in the East Wood Place subdivision, all in one cluster; the Turnpike at the left edge is placed by extension. A hand-picked Pompton / Cedar junction disagreed with the fit by several metres (leave-one-out 10.7 m) and was not used.
The right-hand Turnpike (Pompton) and Grosch have no matching modern line and were not used.
Bradford Avenue appears to be East Bradford and West Bradford Avenue today (not checked against modern junctions).

Sheet 76, 100 ft, rotation about +11 deg. Cedar Grove: Turnpike (Pompton Av), Love Lane (now Bowden Rd), Cedar Av (now Cedar St), East Wood Pl, Union, Summit, Grosch, Bradford Av; one part (the heavy double line is not a part boundary).

sheet-77-1.description: Main part of sheet 77, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering Cedar Grove Center in Verona Township along the Pompton Turnpike. The Turnpike (Pompton Avenue), 66 feet wide, runs down the middle of the sheet. Little Falls Road leaves it eastward near the top and turns north beside Peckmans Brook, Myrtle Avenue is drawn dashed to the west, Grove Avenue runs south-west from the Turnpike, and Love Lane leaves it at the bottom by the bridge over the brook. The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses the sheet just below the centre, with the Cedar Grove Center passenger station west of the Turnpike. Peckmans Brook winds across the lower half and widens into a pond by the railroad. Named works and buildings include the Van Orden Corset Co. on the brook off Little Falls Road, the Cedar Grove Center Hotel on Grove Avenue and a general store and post office on the Turnpike; the rest is scattered frame dwellings and barns. Two insets at 50 feet to an inch, A. Bowden's cotton mill at the Mill Pond (top left) and the ruins of F. J. Marley's hub mill (bottom right), are separate parts.
notes: The Turnpike is modern Pompton Avenue; Love Lane is on the line of modern Bowden Road.
Myrtle Avenue is drawn dashed (not yet opened).
The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad is abandoned.
Placed from four hand-picked junctions all on Pompton Avenue (helmert); rotation comes from the line of Pompton Avenue only. Low confidence.

sheet-79-1.description: Main part of sheet 79, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, covering the land between Fairview Avenue and Grove Avenue north of Personette Avenue in Verona. Fairview Avenue runs down the left side and Grove Avenue down the right; Personette Avenue crosses the bottom, and an unnamed street (lettered Street, no name) runs between Fairview and Grove Avenues a little above it, with a row of narrow lots and frame dwellings between the two. Most of the upper half is the grounds of the Newark City Home for Boys: cottages numbered 1 to 4, a laundry and chapel, a printing and tailor shop, hen houses and other outbuildings, with hydrants and hose marked. F. C. Goble florist, with greenhouses, stands near Grove Avenue. The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad runs along the west edge beyond Fairview Avenue with a small station and wood house. The Newark City Home for Girls is drawn as a boxed inset at 50 feet to an inch in the upper right and is a separate part.
notes: The unnamed street is modern Linden Avenue.
The north part of Fairview Avenue is drawn bending west of its modern line.
The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad is abandoned.

Sheet 79, 100 ft, north toward upper left. Part 1: Fairview Av to Grove Av north of Personette, Street (No Name) = Linden Av, Newark City Home for Boys, F. C. Goble florist. Part 2 (boxed inset, 50 ft): Newark City Home for Girls (elsewhere, no streets).
